name: Kind of Blue
description: Kind of Blue is the 1959 studio album by trumpeter Miles Davis, recorded at Columbia Records' 30th Street Studio in New York City on March 2 and April 22, 1959, and released on August 17, 1959. Davis led a sextet of saxophonists John Coltrane and Julian 'Cannonball' Adderley, bassist Paul Chambers, drummer Jimmy Cobb, and pianists Bill Evans and Wynton Kelly, who plays on one track. Building on the modal experiments of Milestones, Davis based the album entirely on modes rather than chord cycles, handing the musicians brief sketches and scales and capturing mostly first full takes across five compositions: 'So What,' 'Freddie Freeloader,' 'Blue in Green,' 'All Blues,' and 'Flamenco Sketches.' The result redefined what a jazz record could do, influencing jazz, rock, and classical musicians alike. The Library of Congress selected the album for the National Recording Registry in 2002, its inaugural year, and it is routinely described by critics as the greatest jazz album ever made and as Davis's masterpiece.

name: Kerry James Marshall
description: Kerry James Marshall (born October 17, 1955, in Birmingham, Alabama) is a Chicago-based painter whose large-scale figurative paintings place emphatically Black figures at the center of the genres of Western art history. Raised from 1963 in the Watts neighborhood of Los Angeles, he studied at the Otis College of Art and Design, and the painter Charles White — whose studio Marshall had visited as a schoolboy — became his mentor. Marshall has spent much of his career in Chicago: he taught painting at the School of Art and Design of the University of Illinois at Chicago and keeps a studio in Bronzeville. He received a MacArthur Fellowship in 1997. In 2016 the Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago organized Kerry James Marshall: Mastry, a retrospective of roughly eighty works spanning thirty-five years. His 1997 painting Past Times sold at Sotheby's in May 2018 for $21.1 million, then a record for a living African American artist. In 2023 his stained-glass windows Now and Forever were dedicated at Washington National Cathedral.

name: Kane Brown
description: Kane Brown, born Kane Allen Brown on 21 October 1993 in Chattanooga, Tennessee, is an American country singer and songwriter. He is biracial — his mother is white and his father is Black and part Cherokee — and he was raised by his single mother in northwest Georgia and the Chattanooga area, at times experiencing homelessness. First drawn to R&B, he turned to country after winning a school talent contest, sang in a high-school choir alongside Lauren Alaina, and built a mass following posting cover videos on social media. After his debut EP Closer (2015), he signed with RCA Nashville in early 2016 and released his self-titled debut album that December. Its singles “What Ifs,” featuring Alaina, and “Heaven” crossed over, and in October 2017 he became the first artist to hold simultaneous No. 1s on all five main Billboard country charts. Experiment (2018) became his first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200. “One Mississippi” topped Country Airplay ahead of Different Man (2022). His fourth album, The High Road, arrived on 24 January 2025, and he remained active through 2026 with new singles including “Woman” and “Boots.”

name: KaZoom Kids Books
description: KaZoom Kids Books is a Chicago digital-first children's publisher based in Hyde Park, founded by Donna Beasley in 2016 to create greater diversity in children's literature. Its KaZoom Kids iStoryBooks app offers interactive, read-along multicultural picture books for ages 3 to 8 — animation, narration, and stories touching subjects from Black hair to single parenting — on Apple and Android, on a subscription model priced at $75 per year in its launch-era interviews. The company launched with eight titles and a plan of thirty multicultural books in its first year, and it recruits multicultural authors and artists into children's publishing. Coverage includes the Los Angeles Sentinel, Black News, VoyageChicago, and the Support is Sexy podcast.

name: King Von
description: King Von, born Dayvon Daquan Bennett on August 9, 1994, in Chicago, Illinois, was a drill rapper raised in the Parkway Gardens housing complex on the South Side, the area known as O Block around 64th Street and King Drive. A childhood friend of Lil Durk, who urged him to take rap seriously and signed him to his Only the Family label in partnership with Empire, Bennett broke through in 2018 with "Crazy Story," a tightly plotted street narrative that showcased his gift for first-person storytelling. His mixtapes Grandson, Vol. 1 (2019) and Levon James (2020) preceded his debut studio album, Welcome to O'Block, released October 30, 2020. One week later, on November 6, 2020, Bennett, aged 26, was shot and killed in an altercation outside an Atlanta nightclub. His music charted at scale only after his death: Welcome to O'Block rose to No. 5 on the Billboard 200, he earned his first Billboard Hot 100 entries posthumously, and the posthumous album What It Means to Be King (2022) debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200 and No. 1 on Top R&B/Hip-Hop Albums.

name: Kehlani
description: Oakland singer, songwriter and dancer whose forthright, diary-honest writing carried them from teen television to the center of contemporary R&B. Kehlani Ashley Parrish was born on April 24, 1995, in Oakland, California, trained first as a dancer at the Oakland School for the Arts, and first reached a national audience in 2011 as frontperson of the teen group PopLyfe on America's Got Talent. Going solo, they self-released the mixtape Cloud 19 in 2014 and followed it with You Should Be Here (2015), which earned a Grammy nomination for Best Urban Contemporary Album and a deal with Atlantic Records. Their debut studio album SweetSexySavage (2017) peaked at No. 3 on the Billboard 200, and It Was Good Until It Wasn't (2020) reached No. 2, with Blue Water Road (2022) and Crash (2024) extending a catalog marked by candor about love, loss and recovery. In 2025 the single Folded became their first Hot 100 top ten hit, peaking at No. 6, and went on to win two Grammy Awards.

name: Korporate
aliases: Korporate Bidness; Donovan Price Jr.; Donovan Price; I Am Korporate
description: Chicago rapper, comedian, and digital storyteller whose #BlackChicagoBeLike series turned everyday life on the city's South and West sides into one of YouTube's defining Black comedy franchises. Born Donovan Price Jr. in Chicago, he started in music first — spoken word in high school, then rap — and built the Korporate Bidness YouTube channel as a do-it-yourself marketing engine for that music; the comedy skits overtook the songs in reach. He writes, narrates, produces, and stars in the episodes, often casting friends and family, dramatizing neighborhood life with humor and pointed social commentary while deliberately spotlighting Black-owned Chicago businesses, including Woodlawn's Jerk 48. Chicago press documented the rise early: the Chicago Reader profiled him, and the Chicago Sun-Times featured his message-driven stories about marginalized Chicagoans in 2021, noting individual episodes surpassing a million views. As a recording artist he releases through his own Korporate Entertainment — including The Proposal and the single One Uh Dem in 2023, written with composer Wadell Brooks — while framing his long-announced debut album as the work meant to re-establish him as an artist first, the content second.

name: Kamala Harris Sworn In as Vice President (2021)
aliases: Kamala Harris Vice Presidential Inauguration; Harris Becomes Vice President
description: On January 20, 2021, Kamala Harris was sworn in as Vice President of the United States on the West Front of the Capitol, taking the oath from Justice Sonia Sotomayor and becoming — in the intake timeline's exact framing — the first woman and the first Black person, and also the first South Asian American, to hold the office. Harris, the former district attorney of San Francisco, attorney general of California, and United States senator, had been elected on the Democratic ticket with Joseph R. Biden in November 2020. She took the oath using two Bibles, one belonging to Regina Shelton, a childhood neighbor she called a second mother, and one that had belonged to Justice Thurgood Marshall, the first Black Supreme Court justice and a Harris hero. As vice president she held the Senate's tie-breaking vote, casting more of them than any predecessor in the era of the fifty-fifty chamber. Harris herself is held at CTL-E-1481, a sixteen-word stub the audit flagged; this record holds the milestone event, so the graph can cite January 20, 2021, as the date the timeline says it is.

name: Kem
description: Kem (born Kim Lamont Owens, July 23, 1967, in Nashville, Tennessee) is an American R&B singer, songwriter, and producer raised in Detroit and Pontiac, Michigan. After a young adulthood marked by addiction and homelessness, he financed his debut album himself — waiting tables and singing in a wedding band — and self-released Kemistry in 2002, selling some 10,000 copies. Motown Records signed him and re-released Kemistry in February 2003; carried by the single “Love Calls,” the album was certified gold. Working in the quiet-storm tradition of fellow Detroiters Smokey Robinson and Anita Baker, Kem followed with Album II (2005), Intimacy: Album III (2010), Promise to Love (2014), and Love Always Wins (2020), earning multiple Grammy nominations, including two for the single “Why Would You Say.”

description: Kendrick Melvin Nunn (born August 3, 1995, in Chicago, Illinois) is an American professional basketball player from Simeon Career Academy in Chicago, where he wins four straight Illinois state championships alongside Jabari Parker (CTL-E-5586). He plays three seasons at Illinois and finishes his college career at Oakland, where he averages 25.9 points as a senior and wins Horizon League Player of the Year in 2018. After Los Angeles and Washington, and a knee injury that costs him the whole 2021–22 season, he moves to Panathinaikos in October 2023, wins the EuroLeague championship in 2024, and is named EuroLeague MVP in 2025.

name: Kendall Gill
description: Kendall Gill (born Kendall Cedric Gill, May 25, 1968, in Chicago, Illinois) is an American former professional basketball guard and longtime Chicago Bulls broadcaster whose career describes a full Chicago circle — prep star, state-university star, NBA veteran, then the analyst explaining the hometown team on television. At Rich Central High School in Olympia Fields he led his team to a second-place finish in the 1986 IHSA Class AA state tournament. At the University of Illinois (1986–1990) he was a starter on the “Flyin' Illini” team that reached the 1989 Final Four, led the Big Ten in scoring as a senior, and was named a consensus second-team All-American. Drafted fifth overall by the Charlotte Hornets in 1990, he played fifteen NBA seasons for seven teams, made the All-Rookie First Team, and led the NBA in steals in 1998–99. His Chicago playing chapter came with the Bulls in 2003–04; after retirement he became a fixture of Bulls broadcasts, from NBC Sports Chicago to Chicago Sports Network.

name: Kelela
description: Kelela, born Kelela Mizanekristos on June 4, 1983, in Washington, D.C., is an American singer and songwriter and a second-generation Ethiopian American. Raised in Gaithersburg, Maryland, she plays violin in fourth grade, sings in her school choir, and later sings jazz standards at cafés after transferring to American University. She joins the indie band Dizzy Spells in 2008 and moves to Los Angeles in 2010. She makes her recording debut with the 2013 mixtape Cut 4 Me on the Fade to Mind label. Her conceptual EP Hallucinogen follows in 2015, tracing a relationship in reverse chronological order. Her debut studio album, Take Me Apart, released on Warp in 2017, earns wide critical acclaim for blending contemporary R&B with progressive electronic music. After a hiatus, she returns with Raven in February 2023, which she describes as an affirmation of Black femme perspective amid systemic erasure. She remains associated with Warp and Fade to Mind and continues recording and performing internationally.

name: Kel Mitchell
description: Kel Mitchell (born Kel Johari Rice Mitchell on August 25, 1978) is an American actor, comedian, pastor, singer, and writer from Chicago's South Side. A Christian Academy student introduced to theatre at 12, he was cast at 15 in Nickelodeon's sketch series All That, an original cast member from 1994 to 1999, and starred opposite Kenan Thompson in Kenan & Kel and in the film Good Burger (1997), whose Ed became one of the decade's signature characters; a sequel, Good Burger 2, followed in 2023. He voiced T-Bone on Clifford the Big Red Dog, danced on Dancing with the Stars in 2019, and has continued voice and screen work for Nickelodeon. A licensed pastor, he became youth pastor at Spirit Food Christian Center in December 2019 and founded the nonprofit Blessed, Gifted and Black. In 2006 a false report of his death circulated online; Mitchell publicly refuted it, and the claim is preserved in the public record only as a documented hoax. His career joins Chicago comedy lineage to faith leadership and multigenerational children's television.

name: Killer Mike
description: Killer Mike (born Michael Santiago Render on April 20, 1975, in Atlanta, Georgia) is the Adamsville rapper who turned a two-decade underground reputation into a Grammy sweep and an ownership platform. He debuted on Outkast's Stankonia (2000) and won his first Grammy on their "The Whole World" (2003 ceremony), then released Monster (2003) and a run of independent albums before R.A.P. Music (2012), produced by El-P, reset his career; the two formed Run the Jewels in 2013 and released four albums. In 2020 Render co-founded Greenwood, a digital banking platform built for Black and Latino customers — the ownership argument the CTL Short bills — and received Billboard's first Change Maker Award. His autobiographical album Michael (2023), his first solo record in eleven years, swept the rap categories at the February 4, 2024 Grammy Awards: Best Rap Album, and Best Rap Song and Best Rap Performance for "Scientists & Engineers." name: Katori Hall
description: Katori Hall (born May 10, 1981, in Memphis, Tennessee) is an American playwright and television creator. Educated at Columbia University, Harvard's Institute for Advanced Theater Training and the Juilliard School, she broke through with The Mountaintop, her reimagining of Martin Luther King Jr.'s final night at the Lorraine Motel, which premiered in London in 2009, won the Laurence Olivier Award for Best New Play in 2010, and opened on Broadway in 2011. Her comedy The Hot Wing King, premiered at Signature Theatre in 2020, won the 2021 Pulitzer Prize for Drama. For television she created P-Valley (CTL-E-5636), the Starz drama adapted from her own play Pussy Valley, and serves as its showrunner and executive producer through its final season; she also wrote the book for Tina: The Tina Turner Musical, a Tony-nominated production. P-Valley's record in this graph has carried her production credit as a blocked edge since Shorts Wave 4; this record is the endpoint.

name: Kenny Segal
description: Kenny Segal is a Los Angeles-based hip-hop producer, a veteran of the city's Project Blowed underground who came up through the 1990s drum-and-bass scene, whose lush, jazzy, atmospheric production has anchored some of the most acclaimed independent rap records of the past decade. He produced billy woods' Hiding Places (2019) in full for Backwoodz Studioz — an album that topped year-end lists at NPR, Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and Time and was later named one of Rolling Stone's 200 Greatest Hip-Hop Albums of All Time — and the pair followed it with Maps (2023). His Kenstrumentals beat-tape series and production for artists including Open Mike Eagle, R.A.P. Ferreira and Self-Jupiter made him the underground's producer of producers. In 2026 he released DOOMED!, his first full collaborative album with Open Mike Eagle (CTL-E-5562), after nearly twenty years of friendship — the billed duo of CultureTechLens Short #63. Open Mike Eagle's record was minted in Shorts Wave 2 under the duo rule, with Segal named as the further gap; this record is the duo's second principal.

name: Keyshia Cole
description: Keyshia Cole, born Keyshia Myeshia Cole (née Johnson) on 15 October 1981 in Oakland, California, is an American R&B singer dubbed the "Princess of Hip-Hop Soul." Adopted at age two by Leon and Yvonne Cole, she sang backing vocals for MC Hammer as an Oakland youth before relocating to Los Angeles and signing with A&M Records. Her debut The Way It Is (2005) carried "I Should Have Cheated" and "Love" and anchored the BET reality series Keyshia Cole: The Way It Is (2006–08). Just Like You (2007) debuted at No. 2 on the Billboard 200, went platinum, and produced three No. 1 Hot R&B/Hip-Hop singles — "Let It Go," "I Remember" and "Heaven Sent" — earning four Grammy nominations. Her catalogue continues through 11:11 Reset (2017), and she toured North America and the UK in 2025 on The Way It Is 20th Anniversary Tour.

name: Kansas City Monarchs
description: The Kansas City Monarchs were the longest-running and most successful franchise in Negro league baseball, founded in 1920 by owner J. L. Wilkinson, who built the roster from his multiracial All Nations barnstorming club and the Army's 25th Infantry Wreckers. A charter member of the Negro National League in 1920, the club won that league's pennant race repeatedly and took the first Colored World Series in 1924. Wilkinson's portable lighting system made the Monarchs pioneers of night baseball during the Depression. When the Negro American League formed in 1937, the Monarchs became its dominant club, winning five of its first six pennants and eight league titles in all, and the 1942 Negro World Series. The roster line runs through Satchel Paige, Bullet Rogan, Hilton Smith, and Buck O'Neil; in 1945 Wilkinson signed Jackie Robinson, who played one season in Kansas City before Brooklyn. Wilkinson sold the club after 1948; it later moved its base to Grand Rapids, Michigan, while keeping the Monarchs name, and finally disbanded in 1965. Thirteen Monarchs players are in the National Baseball Hall of Fame, and Wilkinson joined them in 2006.

name: Keith David
description: Keith David, born Keith David Williams on 4 June 1956 in Harlem, New York City, and raised in Corona, Queens, is an American actor and Juilliard graduate whose deep voice and screen presence have carried a career of more than four decades. On screen he is known for roles in The Thing (1982), Platoon (1986), They Live (1988) and the drama Greenleaf (2016–2020). As a voice actor he defined a generation of animated characters: Goliath, the lead gargoyle of Disney's Gargoyles (1994–1997), Al Simmons / Spawn in Todd McFarlane's Spawn (1997–1999), and Dr. Facilier, the villain of Disney's The Princess and the Frog (2009). The Television Academy records his Emmy win for Outstanding Voice-Over Performance as narrator of the Ken Burns documentary Unforgivable Blackness: The Rise and Fall of Jack Johnson (2005).

name: Kevin Michael Richardson
description: Kevin Michael Richardson, born 25 October 1964 in the Bronx, New York City, is an American voice actor classically trained at Syracuse University, from which he graduated in 1988. His deep, resonant voice has made him one of the most prolific performers in modern animation, frequently cast as villains and authority figures. Signature roles include Captain Gantu in Disney's Lilo & Stitch franchise (from 2002), the Joker in The Batman (2004–2008), a performance that brought him two Daytime Emmy nominations, and Cleveland Brown Jr. and Lester Krinklesac on The Cleveland Show (2009–2013). His credits run from The Simpsons and Family Guy to the Shredder in the 2012 Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles series and the Mauler Twins and Monster Girl in Invincible (2021–present).

name: Kylian Mbappé
description: Kylian Mbappé, born Kylian Mbappé Lottin on 20 December 1998 in Paris, France, and raised in Bondy, is a French footballer who plays as a forward for Real Madrid and captains the France national team. He began his senior career with Monaco, winning Ligue 1 in 2016–17, then signed for Paris Saint-Germain in 2017, where he won six Ligue 1 titles and became the club's all-time top scorer with 256 goals before joining Real Madrid on a free transfer in 2024. Internationally he won the 2018 FIFA World Cup as a teenager, scoring in the final, and at the 2022 World Cup he scored a hat-trick in the final against Argentina and won the Golden Boot with eight goals, though France lost the final on penalties.

name: Knights of Pythias
aliases: Knights of Pythias of North and South America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia; Knights of Pythias of North America, South America, Europe, Asia, Africa, and Australia; Colored Knights of Pythias; Black Supreme Lodge, Knights of Pythias
description: This record's subject is the Black fraternal order formally named the Knights of Pythias of North and South America, Europe, Asia, Africa and Australia — also known as the Colored Knights of Pythias — and NOT the separate, white Knights of Pythias founded in 1864, which did not allow African Americans to join. Barred from that order, Black founders established their own in Vicksburg, Mississippi, in 1880: Thomas W. Stringer, its first Supreme Chancellor, together with Thomas M. Broadwater, A. E. Lightfoot, George A. Place, W. D. Starks and Claybourne Julian; the first lodge was Lightfoot Lodge No. 1. The order was structured in Supreme Lodge, state Grand Lodges and local lodges, and historically provided members with death and sick benefits. Scholarship counts it among the largest Black fraternal orders. Its women's auxiliary, the Order of Calanthe, was established in Louisiana in 1883. In Birmingham, Alabama, its members anchored a Black business community, provided burial, life and disability insurance, and won a 1912 United States Supreme Court fight over the order's right to exist.

name: Kevin Hart
description: Kevin Darnell Hart (born July 6, 1979, in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania) is an American comedian and actor, raised in Philadelphia by his mother Nancy, who worked as a systems analyst at the University of Pennsylvania. After amateur comedy competitions around New England and a recurring role on the television series Undeclared, he built his reputation through stand-up releases beginning with I'm a Grown Little Man in 2008 and film roles including Think Like a Man (2012), Ride Along (2014), and Central Intelligence (2016). His What Now? tour made him, by Forbes's accounting for June 2015 to June 2016, the highest-paid comedian in the world, ending Jerry Seinfeld's decade at the top of Forbes's list. Time magazine named him to the Time 100, its list of the 100 most influential people in the world, in 2015, and in 2017 he launched the Laugh Out Loud Network in partnership with Lionsgate. Hart remains an active touring comedian and film star in 2026, one of the most commercially successful stand-up performers of his era.

name: Kobe Bryant
description: Kobe Bryant, born Kobe Bean Bryant on 23 August 1978 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, was an American shooting guard who spent his entire 20-year NBA career with the Los Angeles Lakers. The son of NBA player Joe Bryant, he spent part of his childhood in Italy, starred at Lower Merion High School, and went straight to the NBA, chosen by the Charlotte Hornets with the 13th pick of the 1996 draft and traded to the Lakers. With Shaquille O'Neal he won three consecutive championships (2000–02), and he added two more as the team's leader in 2009 and 2010, winning Finals MVP both years; he was league MVP in 2008, an 18-time All-Star, and scored 81 points in a single game in 2006. He retired in 2016 with 33,643 career points and was voted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility. Bryant died in a helicopter crash in Calabasas, California, on 26 January 2020, aged 41, alongside his daughter Gianna and seven others.

name: Kevin Durant
aliases: Kevin Wayne Durant; KD; the Slim Reaper
description: Kevin Durant, born Kevin Wayne Durant on 29 September 1988 in Washington, D.C., is an American professional basketball player for the Houston Rockets. After one season at the University of Texas, where he was the first freshman named Naismith College Player of the Year, he was drafted second overall in 2007 by Seattle and won Rookie of the Year. With the franchise that became the Oklahoma City Thunder he won the league Most Valuable Player award in 2014 and four scoring titles. He joined Golden State in 2016 and won consecutive championships and Finals MVP awards in 2017 and 2018. After an Achilles injury in the 2019 Finals he played for Brooklyn and then Phoenix, passing 30,000 career points with the Suns. In July 2025 Phoenix traded him to Houston in the first seven-team trade in NBA history. In his first Houston season he averaged 26.0 points, and he entered a second Rockets season in October 2026 as the veteran centerpiece of a young roster.

name: Kyrie Irving
description: Kyrie Irving, born Kyrie Andrew Irving on 23 March 1992 in Melbourne, Australia, to American parents and raised in West Orange, New Jersey, is an American professional basketball player for the Dallas Mavericks. After one season at Duke, Cleveland selected him first overall in the 2011 NBA draft and he was named Rookie of the Year. A nine-time All-Star, he won the 2014 All-Star Game MVP award and, in Game 7 of the 2016 NBA Finals, hit the decisive three-pointer that completed Cleveland's comeback against Golden State and delivered the Cavaliers' first championship. He later played for Boston and Brooklyn before a 2023 trade to Dallas, reaching a fourth Finals in 2024. He also won gold with the United States at the 2014 FIBA World Cup, where he was MVP, and at the 2016 Olympics. On 3 March 2025 he tore the ACL in his left knee and missed the whole 2025-26 season; in October 2026 he returned in preseason play in Macao, scoring 17 points against Houston.

name: Kawhi Leonard
description: Kawhi Leonard, born Kawhi Anthony Leonard on 29 June 1991 in Los Angeles, California, is an American forward for the Toronto Raptors and one of the defining two-way players of his era. California's Mr. Basketball at Riverside's Martin Luther King High School, he played two seasons at San Diego State, where his No. 15 was later retired, and was drafted 15th overall in 2011 by Indiana, which traded him to San Antonio on draft night. With the Spurs he won the 2014 championship and Finals MVP and consecutive Defensive Player of the Year awards in 2015 and 2016. Traded to Toronto in 2018, he delivered the Raptors' first championship in 2019, winning a second Finals MVP, then signed with the Los Angeles Clippers, where he played from 2019 to 2026. A seven-time All-Star and member of the NBA 75th Anniversary Team, he was traded back to Toronto on 30 June 2026 and opened the 2026-27 preseason with the Raptors in October 2026. On 2 September 2026 the NBA announced the outcome of its salary-cap circumvention investigation into his Clippers tenure, fining Leonard $700,000 in restitution while imposing larger penalties on the club and its owner.

name: Ken Griffey Jr.
aliases: George Kenneth Griffey Jr.; Junior; The Kid
description: Ken Griffey Jr., born George Kenneth Griffey Jr. on 21 November 1969 in Donora, Pennsylvania, is a Black American former center fielder whose swing and backwards cap defined baseball for a generation. The son of major leaguer Ken Griffey Sr., he was the first overall pick of the 1987 draft and debuted for the Seattle Mariners on 3 April 1989; in 1990 he and his father became the first father and son to play on the same major league team. Traded to his hometown Cincinnati Reds in 2000 and later to the Chicago White Sox, he returned to Seattle before retiring in June 2010 with a .284 average, 2,781 hits, 630 home runs and 1,836 RBIs, plus thirteen All-Star selections, ten Gold Gloves, seven Silver Sluggers and the 1997 American League MVP award. In 2016 he entered the Baseball Hall of Fame with 99.32 percent of the vote, then a record. He later joined the Mariners' ownership group and works as a Mariners special consultant and MLB senior adviser, and in retirement he has built a second career as a credentialed sports photographer.

name: Kenneth B. Clark
description: Kenneth Bancroft Clark was a psychologist and educator whose research with his wife and collaborator, Mamie Phipps Clark, helped change American law. Born in the Panama Canal Zone in 1914 and raised in Harlem, he earned bachelor's and master's degrees at Howard University and, in 1940, a doctorate in psychology from Columbia University. Working from Mamie Clark's master's research on self-identification in Black children, the Clarks developed their celebrated doll experiments, which documented how segregation taught Black children to devalue themselves. Their findings were presented in school desegregation litigation and cited in Brown v. Board of Education in 1954. In 1946 the Clarks founded Harlem's Northside Center for Child Development, a full-time child guidance center. Clark became the first African American tenured full professor at the City College of New York, the first African American president of the American Psychological Association, and the first African American appointed to the New York State Board of Regents. His books include Prejudice and Your Child and Dark Ghetto.

name: Kheris Rogers
description: Kheris Rogers, born in 2006 in Los Angeles, California, is an American fashion entrepreneur and author, the founder of the apparel line Flexin' In My Complexion. Bullied at school for her dark skin — first at a predominantly white school, then, after transferring, through colorism from classmates of her own race — she turned a phrase her grandmother used to affirm her into a brand in 2017, after a photograph her sister Taylor Pollard posted online went viral and drew support from figures including Alicia Keys and Lupita Nyong'o. In September 2017, at eleven years old, she presented the line at Harlem Fashion Week during New York Fashion Week, reported as the youngest designer ever to showcase there. She was named to Teen Vogue's 21 Under 21 list, was selected by LeBron James among the women who inspired his LeBron XVI shoe in 2018, published the picture book Shine Bright in September 2022, and works through the Kheris Rogers Foundation on colorism, representation and youth entrepreneurship. She is an adult, having turned eighteen in 2024 on the sourced 2006 birth year.

name: Killer of Sheep
aliases: Killer of Sheep (1977); Killer of Sheep (1978)
description: Killer of Sheep is a black-and-white American feature written and directed by Charles Burnett, centered on Stan, a Watts slaughterhouse worker whose exhausting job leaves him struggling to provide for his family and to hold onto a dignified life at home. The Museum of Modern Art, which programs the film as a 1977 work of eighty minutes, notes that Burnett made it as his thesis film at UCLA, using school equipment and salvaged 16mm film stock, and that its fragmented, spontaneous scenes offered an authentic portrayal of African American life radically different from the Blaxploitation films of its time. Reference accounts date the shooting primarily to 1972 and 1973, with the completed film submitted as Burnett's Master of Fine Arts thesis in 1977 and premiered at the Whitney Museum of American Art on November 14, 1978 — the source of its alternating 1977 and 1978 datings. Unlicensed music long kept it from general release; it circulated in 16mm until a UCLA restoration and cleared rights brought a wide release in 2007. The Library of Congress lists the film, under release year 1977, as selected for the National Film Registry in 1990.

name: Kahleah Copper
description: Kahleah Copper is an American professional basketball player whose championship run with the Chicago Sky made her a central figure in the city's women's basketball history. A Philadelphia native, she played college basketball at Rutgers University, finishing, according to Rutgers Athletics, third on the program's all-time scoring list with 1,872 points and earning tournament most valuable player honors during Rutgers' 2014 WNIT championship run. Washington selected her seventh overall in the 2016 WNBA draft, and she later joined Chicago, where she moved from a reserve role into the starting lineup. Her defining season came in 2021, when she won her first WNBA All-Star selection, led the Sky through the playoffs, and claimed the WNBA Finals most valuable player award as Chicago defeated Phoenix to win the first championship in franchise history. Rutgers reported that she averaged 17 points and 5.5 rebounds across the four-game Finals. Copper later moved to the Phoenix Mercury. Reporting by the Arizona Republic in April 2026 recorded that Phoenix re-signed her for the 2026 season after she helped the Mercury reach the 2025 WNBA Finals, and the 2026 USA Basketball Women's World Cup roster lists her as a Phoenix Mercury guard-forward from Philadelphia and Rutgers.

name: Karen Jordan
description: Karen Jordan is a Chicago television journalist and anchor-reporter for ABC 7 Chicago (WLS-TV). Secondary biographies that reproduce her station biography report that she joined ABC 7 in July 2003 and co-anchors the station's weekend newscast with Ravi Baichwal. The same biographies trace an Illinois-rooted career: she began as a general assignment reporter at WIFR-TV in Rockford, worked in Dayton, Ohio, at WKEF-TV and WRGT-TV, and then spent 2000 to 2003 as a weekend anchor and general assignment reporter at WPHL-TV in Philadelphia before returning to Chicago. They report her education as a bachelor of arts degree in English from Spelman College in Atlanta in 1994 and a master's degree in broadcast journalism from Northwestern University's Medill School of Journalism in 1995, with early radio experience through the Medill News Service at WMAQ-AM. They also list recognition including a Bethune Recognition for women in the media in 1999, a YMCA Black Achiever Award in 2000, and a 2003 Rising Star designation, plus membership in the National Association of Black Journalists. A journalist index of abc7chicago.com bylines lists articles under her name dated as recently as October 13, 2026, confirming she was actively publishing at ABC 7 in October 2026.

name: Kwame Ture
description: Kwame Ture (June 29, 1941 – November 15, 1998), born Stokely Carmichael in Port of Spain, Trinidad, was a civil rights leader, antiwar activist, and Pan-African revolutionary. His family moved to New York City when he was eleven. He attended Howard University, joined the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee (SNCC) in 1960, and took part in sit-ins and Freedom Rides throughout the Deep South; when SNCC turned to voter registration, he led the campaign that established the Lowndes County Freedom Organization. Elected SNCC's national chairman in May 1966, he popularized “Black Power” on June 16, 1966, at a rally in Greenwood, Mississippi, during the continued March Against Fear, defining the term as a call for Black people to unite, recognize their heritage, build community, define their own goals, and lead their own organizations. The Black Panther Party named him its Honorary Prime Minister in 1968. He changed his name to Kwame Ture in honor of Pan-African leaders Kwame Nkrumah of Ghana and Sékou Touré of Guinea, settled permanently in Conakry, Guinea in 1969, and spent his last decades building the All-African People's Revolutionary Party. He died of prostate cancer in Conakry in 1998, aged 57.

name: Kasi Lemmons
description: Kasi Lemmons is an American film director, screenwriter, actress, librettist and educator. Born Karen Diane Lemmons in St. Louis, Missouri, to biology teacher Milton Lemmons and Dorothy Lemmons, a counsellor who later became a psychologist, she was raised largely in Newton, Massachusetts, after her parents' divorce, performed with the Boston Children's Theatre, and studied at New York University's Tisch School of the Arts, at the University of California, Los Angeles — where she majored in history — and in the film programme at the New School for Social Research. She acted first, debuting in the 1979 television movie 11th Victim, playing Ardelia Mapp in The Silence of the Lambs (1991), and appearing in School Daze and Candyman. She then wrote Eve's Bayou and directed it herself: released in 1997, the Louisiana family drama won the Independent Spirit Award for Best First Feature, earned a National Board of Review debut honour, was the highest-grossing independent film of 1997, and entered the National Film Registry in 2018. Five further features followed — The Caveman's Valentine (2001), Talk to Me (2007), Black Nativity (2013), Harriet (2019) and Whitney Houston: I Wanna Dance with Somebody (2022) — alongside television work including Self Made (2020). Her libretto for Terence Blanchard's opera Fire Shut Up in My Bones opened the Metropolitan Opera's 2021–22 season — the first Met opera by an African American composer and librettist — and won the Grammy Award for Best Opera Recording. Lemmons is an Arts Professor in the Graduate Film Department at NYU Tisch, and in 2025 she received the Los Angeles Press Club's Distinguished Storyteller Award.

name: Karen Fields-Lever
description: Dr. Karen Fields-Lever is the owner and founder of 28 to Brush Dental Studio (28 to BRUSH), the Forest Park, Illinois dental practice she opened in 2014, providing general and cosmetic care together with a mobile dentistry program — launched in 2016 and reported to have served more than 16,000 students — in schools and community centers. A Spelman College and Howard University College of Dentistry graduate, she completed a residency at Yale. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kalia Coleman
description: Kalia Coleman is a Partner at Riley Safer Holmes & Cancila LLP (RSHC), the Chicago-headquartered national litigation firm founded in 2016, practicing in government enforcement, investigations and white-collar criminal defense. She joined RSHC after nearly six years as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Illinois, most recently as Deputy Chief of the General Crimes Division, and previously served as an Assistant State's Attorney in the Cook County State's Attorney's Office. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kenneth Griffin
description: Kenneth Griffin is the founder of No Matter What, a Chicago 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded in Englewood in 2015 that invests in Chicagoland youth through mentorship, career readiness, mental-health healing, a community garden, culinary camp and summer travel. DePaul University identifies him as a DePaul graduate (SCPS '25, in nonprofit management), a Chicago police officer and chef who received the American Red Cross of Greater Chicago's Law Enforcement Hero award. He is not Kenneth C. Griffin, the Citadel founder and investor. He was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Kiearrah Lawrence
description: Kiearrah Lawrence is an AbbVie marketing leader credited on WVON's roster as Associate Director, Marketing; the Healthcare Businesswomen's Association named her a 2026 Rising Star for AbbVie Inc. Indiana University's 2022 coverage of the Kelley Direct Online MBA placed her in AbbVie finance and accounting while leading the company's African American employee resource group, the Black Business Network — the marketing directorship the roster records is her current role. She was named to WVON's 40 Under 40 Game Changers Class of 2026.

name: Krista Whitaker
description: Krista Whitaker is Executive Vice President of Legal and Business Affairs and Chief Legal Officer of the Chicago Bears, appointed April 9, 2024; the club states she leads its legal and security departments and works closely with President & CEO Kevin Warren across football and business operations. She joined the Bears from the Miami Heat, where she rose from Senior Associate Counsel (2021) to Vice President & Associate General Counsel, after roughly five years as a sports-law corporate associate at Proskauer Rose; she earned her JD at Stanford Law School in 2015 and was honored in 2025 by the Black Women Lawyers' Association of Greater Chicago. description: Kyle Gardner is CEO and Co-Founder of Dobson Avenue Capital Partners, LLC, a private investment firm supporting underrepresented entrepreneurs — the title given by Autism Speaks, where he chairs the Upper Midwest leadership council, and by the 2020 launch of The Empower Project for Black-owned consumer-goods businesses, in which Dobson Avenue provided advisory guidance and monetary investment.
